title: 7.10.1: Profile data structures and serde YAML support
description:
## Scope

Add serde_yaml dependency and define core Rust types for Profile system. Profile struct with name, description, priority, match (MatchExpr), extraction (ExtractionOverrides), fields (FieldMap). MatchExpr enum with All, Any, None variants containing Vec<Predicate>. Predicate enum for all 11 kinds (TextContains, TextMatches, HeadingMatches, HasCurrencyPattern, HasSignatureField, Structural). Structural predicate with sub-predicates (page_count, has_table, has_form_field, has_math, heading_depth, font_diversity). ExtractionOverrides struct for tuning (reading_order, table_detection, readability_threshold, include_invisible, include_headers_footers, force_ocr, min_block_chars). Field struct with localizers (near, region, pick, max_distance_pt) and extractors (regex, parse). FieldMap (BTreeMap<String, Field>). PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN constant: forbidden top-level keys.

## Why this matters

Foundation for entire Profile system. serde_yaml enables YAML loading. Well-defined types ensure type-safe profile evaluation and make the DSL explicit in the type system.

## Implementation guidance

- Feature flag: profiles (adds serde_yaml = "0.9")
- Profile, MatchExpr, Predicate, StructuralPredicate, ExtractionOverrides, Field, FieldMap structs in crates/pdftract-core/src/profiles/mod.rs
- Deserialize YAML to Profile; profile_version: "1.0.0" hardcoded
- PROFILE_SECRETS_FORBIDDEN: HashSet of forbidden keys; validate during deserialization
- Add profiles module to pdftract-core lib.rs
- serde attributes for field renaming (snake_case to camelCase as needed)
- Unit tests for Profile deserialization from valid YAML
- Unit tests for forbidden keys rejection

## Acceptance criteria

- Profile type compiles with serde_yaml enabled
- Valid YAML deserializes to Profile correctly
- Forbidden top-level keys rejected with error
- Unit tests pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 Profile YAML schema (lines 2912-2961)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.2: Match DSL evaluator
description:
## Scope

Implement evaluator for MatchExpr against DocumentSignals. Evaluate All (all must match), Any (at least one must match), None (none must match). Predicate evaluators: text_contains (checks full document text), text_matches (regex), heading_matches (regex against heading blocks), has_currency_pattern (currency regex), has_signature_field (AcroForm sig field check), structural (delegates to StructuralPredicate evaluator). StructuralPredicate evaluators: page_count (range check), has_table (check block kinds), has_form_field (check AcroForm fields), has_math (check math operators), heading_depth (max depth of heading hierarchy), font_diversity (count distinct font names).

## Why this matters

Match DSL is how profiles find their target documents. Accurate matching is critical for applying the right extraction heuristics.

## Implementation guidance

- DocumentSignals struct in profiles/signals.rs: snapshot of document properties (full_text, heading_texts, page_count, block_kinds, has_form_fields, has_signature_fields, has_math, heading_depth, font_names)
- MatchEvaluator in profiles/evaluator.rs: evaluate(&MatchExpr, &DocumentSignals) -> bool
- Each predicate gets its own evaluation method
- Regex caching for text_matches and heading_matches (compile once, reuse)
- Currency pattern regex: \$\d|€\d|£\d|¥\d|USD\d|EUR\d|GBP\d
- Unit tests for each predicate kind
- Unit tests for combinator logic (all/any/none)
- Integration test: full profile YAML against DocumentSignals

## Acceptance criteria

- All 11 predicate kinds evaluate correctly
- Combinators (all/any/none) work correctly
- Regex patterns compile and match as expected
- Currency pattern detects common currency formats
- Unit and integration tests pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 Match DSL primitives (lines 2963-2980)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.3: Field DSL evaluator
description:
## Scope

Implement evaluator for Field extraction. Localizers: near (find anchor spans containing strings, restrict candidates within max_distance_pt), region (filter by page region: top_quarter, bottom_quarter, left_half, right_half, top:N, bottom:N, bbox:[x0,y0,x1,y1]), pick (disambiguate: largest_font, smallest_font, nearest_below, nearest_right, first, last). Extractors: regex (apply to candidate text, capture group 1 or 0), parse (decimal, date, int, bool with heuristic format detection). Fields evaluate in document order; first hit per field wins.

## Why this matters

Field DSL extracts structured data (invoice_number, total, vendor, etc.) from documents. This is the value-add of profiles beyond just tuning extraction.

## Implementation guidance

- FieldEvaluator in profiles/field_evaluator.rs
- SpanCandidates struct: holds extracted spans with metadata (text, bbox, font_size)
- Localizer implementations:
  - near: search spans for anchor strings, find candidates within distance
  - region: geometric filtering by page region
  - pick: disambiguation heuristics
- Extractor implementations:
  - regex: apply to candidate text, return captured value
  - parse: type parsing with format detection
- Field extraction returns HashMap<String, serde_json::Value> (null when not found)
- Unit tests for each localizer
- Unit tests for each extractor
- Integration test: full field extraction from sample document

## Acceptance criteria

- All localizers work correctly
- All extractors work correctly
- Field extraction returns correct structured data
- null returned when field not found (no error)
- Unit and integration tests pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 Field-extraction DSL (lines 2994-3006)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.4: Profile loader with search path
description:
## Scope

Implement profile loader that walks search path in priority order. Load order: built-in (compiled via include_str!), /etc/pdftract/profiles/*.yaml, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pdftract/profiles/*.yaml, --profile-dir DIR (repeatable). Later profiles shadow earlier on name collision. Built-in profiles embedded in binary. User profiles loaded from disk. Invalid profiles logged and skipped. Profile resolution returns highest-priority matching profile.

## Why this matters

Profile loader is how profiles become available. Search path enables layering: ship built-ins, admins override in /etc, users override in ~/.config, runtime override via --profile-dir.

## Implementation guidance

- ProfileLoader in profiles/loader.rs
- Built-in profiles via include_str!("profiles/builtin/*.yaml")
- etc path: /etc/pdftract/profiles/
- XDG path: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config/pdftract/profiles/
- --profile-dir CLI flag (repeatable) parsed and passed to loader
- load() method returns HashMap<String, Profile> (name -> profile)
- Shadowing: later insert overwrites earlier on same name
- Invalid YAML: log warning, skip file, continue
- resolve_best_match(doc_signals, loaded_profiles) -> Option<(Profile, f32)>
- Confidence calculation: predicate count satisfied / total predicates
- Unit tests for search path ordering
- Unit tests for shadowing behavior
- Unit tests for invalid profile handling

## Acceptance criteria

- Built-in profiles load correctly
- User profiles load from XDG and --profile-dir
- Shadowing works (later wins on name collision)
- Invalid profiles logged and skipped
- resolve_best_match picks highest-priority profile with confidence >= 0.6
- Unit tests pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 Profile resolution and search path (lines 3040-3051)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.5: Extraction tuning integration
description:
## Scope

Apply ExtractionOverrides from matched profile to ExtractionOptions. When profile matches, merge profile extraction block with default options. Override fields: reading_order, table_detection, readability_threshold, include_invisible, include_headers_footers, force_ocr, min_block_chars. Profile fields take precedence over defaults. Unknown extraction keys logged with warning but don't error (forward compat).

## Why this matters

Extraction tuning is the core value of profiles. Different document types need different reading order strategies (invoices line-by-line, papers two-column). Profiles enable this without code changes.

## Implementation guidance

- apply_extraction_tuning(profile: &Profile, opts: &mut ExtractionOptions) in profiles/tuning.rs
- For each extraction field, if profile sets it, override opts
- reading_order: parse string to enum variant
- table_detection: parse string to enum variant
- readability_threshold: f32
- include_invisible: bool
- include_headers_footers: bool
- force_ocr: bool
- min_block_chars: usize
- Log warning for unknown extraction keys (forward compat)
- Unit tests for each override field
- Integration test: full profile application changes extraction behavior

## Acceptance criteria

- All extraction override fields apply correctly
- Unknown keys logged with warning, don't error
- ExtractionOptions mutated correctly
- Unit and integration tests pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 Extraction tuning keys (lines 2982-2993)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.6: CLI profiles subcommand (list, show, export, install, validate)
description:
## Scope

Implement pdftract profiles subcommand with 5 subcommands. list: show all profiles (built-in + user), annotate shadowing with "(overrides built-in)". show NAME: dump profile YAML to stdout. export NAME: copy built-in profile YAML to stdout. install YAML_FILE: install to ~/.config/pdftract/profiles/. validate YAML_FILE: syntax + schema check, no extraction, report errors with line numbers.

## Why this matters

profiles subcommand gives users a way to inspect, export, install, and validate profiles. Essential for operational workflow.

## Implementation guidance

- profiles.rs module in pdftract-cli
- Clap subcommand: ProfilesSubcommand with list, show, export, install, validate variants
- list: walk search path, print profiles with annotations
- show: load profile by name, print YAML
- export: load built-in profile, print YAML
- install: read YAML, write to ~/.config/pdftract/profiles/<name>.yaml
- validate: load YAML, report errors with line numbers, exit 0 if valid
- Create ~/.config/pdftract/profiles/ if doesn't exist (for install)
- Unit tests for each subcommand
- Integration tests for list output format
- Integration tests for validate error reporting

## Acceptance criteria

- All 5 subcommands work correctly
- list shows shadowing annotation
- validate reports errors with line numbers
- install creates directory if needed
- Unit and integration tests pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 CLI (lines 3026-3038)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.7: CLI extract --auto and --profile flags
description:
## Scope

Add --auto and --profile flags to pdftract extract. --auto: evaluate all profiles, pick highest-priority match with confidence >= 0.6, apply extraction tuning, emit profile metadata. --profile NAME|PATH: force-apply named profile or YAML file, skip matching, apply extraction tuning, emit profile metadata. Output adds metadata.profile_name, metadata.profile_version, metadata.profile_fields to JSON.

## Why this matters

--auto enables automatic document classification and extraction tuning. --profile enables manual override. Both emit extracted fields in metadata.

## Implementation guidance

- Add --auto and --profile flags to extract subcommand in pdftract-cli
- --auto and --profile mutually exclusive (error if both set)
- --auto flow: load profiles, evaluate all, pick best match, apply tuning, extract fields
- --profile NAME: load named profile from search path, apply
- --profile PATH: load YAML file directly, apply
- Add profile metadata to output JSON (profile_name, profile_version, profile_fields)
- profile_fields: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>, null for missing fields
- Integration test: --auto on invoice fixture
- Integration test: --profile on sample PDF
- Integration test: output JSON contains profile metadata

## Acceptance criteria

- --auto classifies document and applies best profile
- --profile applies specified profile
- Profile metadata emitted in JSON
- --auto and --profile are mutually exclusive
- Integration tests pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 CLI (lines 3028-3032)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.8: Built-in profiles (invoice, receipt, contract, scientific_paper, slide_deck, form, bank_statement, legal_filing, book_chapter)
description:
## Scope

Create 9 built-in profile YAML files in profiles/builtin/. invoice, receipt, contract, scientific_paper, slide_deck, form, bank_statement, legal_filing, book_chapter. Each with match predicates, extraction tuning, and field extractors. Each with >= 5 fixture documents in tests/fixtures/profiles/<name>/. Regression tests for each profile.

## Why this matters

Built-in profiles give users out-of-the-box support for common document types. Fixtures ensure profiles work correctly and prevent regressions.

## Implementation guidance

- profiles/builtin/invoice.yaml, receipt.yaml, contract.yaml, scientific_paper.yaml, slide_deck.yaml, form.yaml, bank_statement.yaml, legal_filing.yaml, book_chapter.yaml
- Each profile: match predicates, extraction tuning, fields
- invoice: invoice_number, vendor, customer, invoice_date, due_date, total, subtotal, tax, line_items
- receipt: merchant, date, total, tax, items, payment_method
- contract: parties, effective_date, term, governing_law, signatures
- scientific_paper: title, authors, abstract, doi, journal, publication_date, references
- slide_deck: title, presenter, date, slide_titles
- form: reading_order = line_dominant, no fields (surfaces Phase 7.4 form_fields)
- bank_statement: account_number, statement_period, opening_balance, closing_balance, transactions
- legal_filing: case_number, court, parties, filing_date, docket_entries
- book_chapter: title, chapter_number, author, sections
- Fixtures in tests/fixtures/profiles/<name>/ (>= 5 each)
- Regression tests for each profile in tests/profiles/<name>.rs
- 50-invoice fixture corpus for invoice profile (acceptance criterion)

## Acceptance criteria

- 9 built-in profile YAML files exist
- Each profile has match, extraction, fields sections
- Each profile has >= 5 fixtures
- Regression tests pass for each profile
- Invoice profile >= 90% field accuracy on 50-invoice corpus

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 Built-in profiles (lines 3053-3067)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.9: serve --profile-hot-reload with inotify
description:
## Scope

Add --profile-dir and --profile-hot-reload flags to pdftract serve. --profile-dir DIR: load profiles from directory. --profile-hot-reload: re-read DIR on every request (inotify-watched; polling fallback on platforms without inotify). New YAML picked up on next request without restart.

## Why this matters

Hot-reload lets operators iterate on profiles without restarting serve. Critical for production workflows.

## Implementation guidance

- Add notify dependency for inotify support
- --profile-dir flag (repeatable) to serve subcommand
- --profile-hot-reload flag to serve subcommand
- When hot-reload enabled: re-read profiles on every request
- inotify watcher: detect file changes, invalidate cache
- Polling fallback: check mtime on every request (no inotify)
- Profile cache: HashMap<String, Profile>, invalidated on change
- Integration test: drop new YAML, next request picks it up
- Integration test: profile change detected without restart

## Acceptance criteria

- --profile-dir loads profiles from directory
- --profile-hot-reload re-reads on every request
- New YAML picked up on next request
- inotify used when available, polling fallback otherwise
- Integration tests pass

## References

- Plan section: 7.10 Hot-reload (line 3069)
- Bead: pdftract-3a310 (parent coordinator)

title: 7.10.10: Critical tests and validation
description:
